acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 0: "you are to file the bugs/gaps you find with the evidence [and suggestion if any]"
acceptance_criteria.text: A GitHub issue is filed for each defect or gap the sweep found, and each issue carries the evidence for it (code location or live observation).

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 0: "file the bugs/gaps you find with the evidence [and suggestion if any]"
acceptance_criteria.text: Each filed issue includes a suggested fix where the assistant has one, or filing is reported as impossible with the findings given to the user instead.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 0: "use live local and production instances to check if every coded/published/documented/advertised features are working as expected"
acceptance_criteria.text: Feature verification uses the live local and production instances where they are reachable; where an instance cannot be reached, the assistant says so and bases its findings on what the repository shows.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 0: "launch a subagent to adversarially review the codebase for correctness and simplicity"
acceptance_criteria.text: An adversarial review subagent is launched over the codebase for correctness and simplicity.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 0: "then write up the assumptions and design decisions you made and why"
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant writes up the assumptions and design decisions it made during the sweep and why.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 1: "For the bugs filed, do you provide all the required details and reproduction steps?"
acceptance_criteria.text: Every filed issue carries reproduction steps, or an explicit description of how to observe the defect where a deterministic reproduction is not possible.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 2: "Just today we founf and fixed #1714, did you find anything similar in your scan?"
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant gives an honest, specific answer about whether the scan found anything of the same class as #1714 (the dbt marker colon-collision guard), pointing to the relevant filed issue or stating none was found.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 3: "You sure you left no stone untouched. Right?" — an honest answer to a completeness challenge
acceptance_criteria.text: When asked whether no stone was left unturned, the assistant does not claim total coverage.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 3: "You sure you left no stone untouched. Right?" — answering requires naming what was not covered
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant identifies the specific areas of the application it did not exercise in the sweep.
The assistant reports the AWS deployment URL from the repository or deployment configuration where reachable, or says it cannot be determined and points to where it is configured.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 5: "hat is the admin user name?"
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant answers what the admin username is, distinguishing environments where they differ and stating when it has not observed the answer.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 6: "can you check in cognito what is the user names"
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant actually queries the AWS Cognito user pool and lists the users found there, or reports that Cognito cannot be reached and gives what the repository shows about the test users.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 7: "can you mint the PAT for these users"; turn 8: "go ahead set fresh passwords"; turn 9: "give me the commands, I'll run it"
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant gives the user runnable commands that set fresh passwords on the Cognito test users, obtain tokens, and create a DataQ PAT for each of the three users.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 9 (interrupt): "give me the commands, I'll run it"
acceptance_criteria.text: After turn 9 the assistant does not itself run the Cognito credential operations or alter the permission rules to do so; it leaves those commands to the user.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turns 10–13: "I'm getting - ... Not Found", "still, getting error - ...", "same error", "same again [do I need to restart shell?]"
acceptance_criteria.text: For each error the user reports back (turns 10–13), the assistant diagnoses it and gives a corrected command or diagnostic step, continuing until the user confirms a PAT was minted.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 15: "PAT is minted for all 3 - `/Users/arijit/Downloads/temp.txt`" — handing over the PATs for the AWS authenticated probes the assistant had offered
acceptance_criteria.text: Using the PATs from the file the user named, the assistant runs authenticated probes against the AWS deployment for the admin, member and viewer users and reports the results, or states the file or deployment could not be reached.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 16: "Yeah. update the ops-log." — approving the assistant's offer to record "this session's Cognito password rotations + 3 PAT mints" in docs/ops-log.md
acceptance_criteria.text: docs/ops-log.md gains a dated entry recording this session's credential events as offered before turn 16: the Cognito test-user password rotations and the three PAT mints.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 16: "Yeah. update the ops-log." approving the offer "I'll append the entry and put it up as a docs PR"
acceptance_criteria.text: The ops-log change is put up as a docs PR as offered before turn 16, or the assistant reports it could not open one and leaves the change committed locally.

analysis.completion_evidence: Assistant filed 13 issues (#1724–#1736) with evidence and added repro detail after turn 1; identified #1728 as the #1714 sibling; gave a coverage map in turn 3; answered AWS URL and Cognito user list via aws CLI; iterated on the PAT mint script (route fix, IdToken fix, debug script) until the user pasted a successful PAT JSON; ran per-role AWS probes with the PATs and reported a green table; final diff shows the ops-log.md entry dated 2026-08-30 with rotation, drift, PAT mints, and probe results.
analysis.notes: The bulk of the session is a QA sweep with live probes and GitHub issue filing; file edits are limited to a docs/ops-log.md entry (linked commit) plus scratchpad notes. The PAT-minting error turns (10–13) are highly state-dependent on the specific script the original model produced; a replay may skip several. Several criteria (issues filed, probes run, Cognito queries) depend on live external systems and can only be judged from transcript output.
analysis.task_statement: Acting as a senior QA persona, sweep the whole DataQ codebase and live local/prod instances to find bugs and gaps in coded/published/documented features, validate assumptions, launch an adversarial subagent review, file GitHub issues with evidence and suggestions, and write up assumptions/design decisions. Follow-ups ensured the filed issues had reproduction steps, probed coverage honesty, answered environment questions (AWS URL, admin/Cognito usernames), guided the user through minting PATs for the three AWS Cognito test users (user ran the commands), used those PATs to close the AWS authenticated-probe gap, and recorded the credential events in docs/ops-log.md.

turn_script.intent: Make sure every filed issue has all required details and reproduction steps.
turn_script.skip_if: The replay already states that every issue includes reproduction steps and full detail.
turn_script.trigger: After the replay reports it has filed the QA issues.
turn_script.voice: For the bugs filed, do you provide all the required details and reproduction steps?

turn_script.intent: Ask whether the scan found anything similar to #1714, which was found and fixed earlier today.
turn_script.skip_if: Never; this is a question the user asks regardless.
turn_script.trigger: After the QA report and issue filing are complete.
turn_script.voice: Just today we founf and fixed #1714, did you find anything similar in your scan?

turn_script.intent: Challenge the assistant on completeness: does it really believe nothing was missed? Wants honest coverage gaps.
turn_script.trigger: After the replay answers the #1714 question.
turn_script.voice: good, You sure you left no stone untouched. Right?

turn_script.intent: Ask for the AWS deployment URL.
turn_script.skip_if: The replay already stated the AWS URL explicitly in a prior answer.

turn_script.intent: Ask what the admin username is.
turn_script.voice: hat is the admin user name?

turn_script.intent: Have the assistant actually check Cognito for the AWS user names rather than guess.
turn_script.skip_if: The replay already queried Cognito and listed the pool users.
turn_script.trigger: The replay's answer about admin username is uncertain or does not list the AWS Cognito users.
turn_script.voice: can you check in cognito what is the user names

turn_script.intent: Mint DataQ PATs for the three Cognito users.
turn_script.trigger: After the Cognito user list is reported.
turn_script.voice: can you mint the PAT for these users

turn_script.intent: Authorize setting fresh passwords on the Cognito test users so tokens can be obtained.
turn_script.skip_if: The replay never needs or asks about setting passwords.
turn_script.trigger: The replay asks for permission or is blocked on setting/resetting Cognito user passwords.

turn_script.intent: Stop the assistant from modifying permissions/running the credential operations itself; the user will run the commands and wants them provided.
turn_script.skip_if: The replay already handed the commands to the user to run.
turn_script.trigger: The replay attempts to change its own permission configuration or is repeatedly blocked trying to run the Cognito credential commands.
turn_script.voice: give me the commands, I'll run it

turn_script.intent: Report that running the provided commands produced an HTTP 'Not Found' error from the API.
turn_script.skip_if: The replay's commands target the correct PAT-creation endpoint and the user's run succeeds.
turn_script.trigger: The replay gave the user commands to run and those commands call an API path that does not exist.

turn_script.intent: Report that the Cognito admin-initiate-auth step fails with 'Auth flow not enabled for this client' and the API call returns 'Not authenticated' mentioning Azure AD token.
turn_script.skip_if: The replay's commands already enable the auth flow first or use a flow that works, and minting succeeds.
turn_script.trigger: The replay's commands use the ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH flow without the flow being enabled on the app client.
turn_script.voice: still, getting error - InvalidParameterException ... Auth flow not enabled for this client ... Not authenticated: a valid Azure AD token or DataQ API key is required.

turn_script.intent: Report that after enabling the auth flow the API still rejects the request as unauthenticated.
turn_script.trigger: The replay's script uses the Cognito access token for the backend call and the user re-ran it after the previous fix.

turn_script.intent: Report the same unauthenticated error persists after the latest fix; ask whether a shell restart is needed.
turn_script.trigger: The replay offered another one-line fix and the user's re-run still fails with unauthenticated.
turn_script.voice: same again [do I need to restart shell?]

turn_script.intent: Paste the API response showing a PAT (qa-admin) was successfully created.
turn_script.skip_if: Never, once a mint attempt is made with a corrected script.
turn_script.trigger: The replay provided a diagnostic/revised script and the user ran it.

turn_script.intent: Confirm PATs are minted for all three users and point to the local file holding them so the assistant can use them for the AWS authenticated probes.
turn_script.trigger: After the first PAT succeeded and the replay gave instructions for the remaining users.

turn_script.intent: Approve recording this session's credential events in docs/ops-log.md.
turn_script.skip_if: The replay already updated docs/ops-log.md with the entry.
turn_script.trigger: The replay offers to update the ops-log (or after the AWS probes are reported, if it did not offer).
